snippets.output: A short-term solution for insomnia can be achieved through a combination of behavioral and lifestyle modifications.

Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is a non-pharmacological approach that has been shown to be effective in reducing symptoms of insomnia, and it typically involves a combination of techniques such as sleep restriction, stimulus control, and cognitive restructuring.

Establishing a consistent sleep schedule and creating a relaxing bedtime routine can help improve sleep quality. A relaxing bedtime routine can include reading a book, taking a warm bath, or practicing gentle stretches before bedtime.

Another short-term solution for insomnia is the use of sleep aids such as melatonin supplements; melatonin is a hormone that regulates sleep-wake cycles. Taking a small dose of melatonin (0.5–1 mg) 30 minutes before bedtime may help improve sleep quality.

It is essential to consult with a healthcare professional before taking any sleep aids designed as a short-term solution for insomnia, because sleep aids can interact with other medications and can have side effects.
